verdict: DoorDash set records across the board — orders up 28%, the value of goods ordered up 36% to $33.9B — and net income nearly doubled to $465M as the delivery machine scaled.

segments.name: Marketplace services
segments.note: Commissions from restaurants and stores, delivery fees, and DashPass/Wolt+ memberships across DoorDash's marketplaces (including Wolt and Deliveroo). DoorDash reports one revenue stream.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing and promotions to win diners, merchants and couriers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the delivery platform, including AI and autonomy work.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear on equipment, vehicles and software — the part not counted inside cost of revenue.

takeaways.title: The marketplace keeps compounding
takeaways.text: Gross order value rose 36% to $33.9B on 993M orders. DoorDash keeps only a slice of each order — $4.6B of revenue from $33.9B of goods is the whole model in one line.

takeaways.title: Profit is scaling now
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $465M from $243M a year ago — revenue grew 34% while most cost lines grew slower. That is the operating leverage delivery was always supposed to produce.

takeaways.title: EPS doubled
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS was $1.06 vs $0.55 a year ago. The release also flags a proposed acquisition of Instacart — the next chapter, if shareholders and regulators agree.

otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$42M — $37M of interest earned on cash, plus $5M of other income.
footerNote: DoorDash reports cost of revenue before depreciation. The $134M of depreciation tied to cost of revenue is included in cost above, so the gross profit shown ($2,311M) matches DoorDash's published figure. Net income attributable to DoorDash stockholders was $466M (a $1M loss sat with non-controlling interests).
